sourceTitle: LROC Lunar Pit Atlas (Arizona State University)
unitSource: USGS Unified Geologic Map of the Moon, 1:5,000,000 (Fortezzo, Spudis and Harrel 2020)
nullPolicy: Keep N/A as unavailable; greater-than depths remain bounds, not exact measurements.
note: Longitudes converted from 0-360 east to -180..180. Depths written as '>N' in the atlas are lower bounds, not measurements. The map unit is the smallest USGS polygon containing the pit centre; at 1:5M scale it describes the surrounding terrain, not the pit.

Cc.name: Copernican Crater
Cc.description: Rim, wall and floor deposits of craters with sharp prominent rims, circular to polygonal outlines. High relative brightness and rays.

Ec.name: Eratosthenian Crater
Ec.description: Non-rayed, circular craters with sharp to partially subdued crater rim crests, partial circumferential ejecta present, and lower albedo compared to unit Cc.
Ec.interpretation: Morphology and material from a primary impact event.

Im2.name: Imbrian Mare, Upper
Im2.description: Forms flat, smooth surfaces. Lower albedo and crater density than unit Im1. Numerous ridges. Difficult to distinguish from unit Id.

Ip.name: Imbrian Plains
Ip.description: Smooth, flat to undulatory terrain of intermediate albedo occurring mostly in topographic lows and crater floors of Imbrian and older age.
Ip.interpretation: Ambiguous origin, likely Orientale and other large impact crater ejecta.

Ib.name: Imbrian Basin, Undivided
Ib.description: Gently rolling to hilly terrain containing aggregates of subdued irregular to circular craters. Also forms outer basin and ejecta of crater Schrodinger.
Ib.interpretation: Materials emplaced during the formation of multi-ringed impact basins.

Nt.name: Nectarian Terra
Nt.description: Moderately rough surface, rolling to moderately rugged overall relief, with diverse ages of superposed and buried craters.
Nt.interpretation: Complex mixture of local erosional debris and crater and basin ejecta; megaregolith.

Ic2.name: Imbrian Crater, Upper
Ic2.description: Similar description to unit Ic, craters superpose materials of the Orientale group.
Ic2.interpretation: Subdued morphology and material from a primary impact event, younger than Orientale group materials but older than unit Im2.

Iia.name: Imbrian Imbrium Alpes Formation
Iia.description: Angular blocky and knobby with smooth, mantled surface. Closely spaced hills and hummocks, ~2-5 km in diameter.
Iia.interpretation: Possibly eroded ejecta, structurally deformed bedrock, or both.

Ic1.name: Imbrian Crater, Lower
Ic1.description: Similar description to unit Ic, craters mantled by materials of the Orientale group.
Ic1.interpretation: Subdued morphology and material from a primary impact event, younger than Imbrium group materials but older than Orientale group materials.

EIp.name: Eratosthenian Imbrian Plateau
EIp.description: Forms high standing plateaus (relative to the mare surfaces in Oceanus Procellarum) with domes, cones, and dark mantling materials.
EIp.interpretation: Volcanic constructs, flows, and pyroclastic materials.

pNt.name: pre-Nectarian Terra
pNt.description: Rugged, diverse terrain, degraded partial crater rims, gradational with smoother unit Nt, and rougher units pNbm and pNc.
pNt.interpretation: Complex mixture of local erosional debris and crater and basin ejecta; megaregolith.

Nc.name: Nectarian Crater
Nc.description: Considerably muted topographic relief compared to younger impact features, with broad flat floors typically another unit, and very little to no ejecta present.
Nc.interpretation: Muted morphology and material from a primary impact event.
